stage_j.discrepancy_explanation: The historical multi-token disclosure across reports S0-2 through S0-6 was evaluated on bare object strings without leading space (tokenizer.encode(f['object'].strip())). In GPT-2 byte-pair encoding, bare strings lack the leading space character byte, causing common entity words to be split into multiple sub-word tokens. In the actual training and evaluation execution path (b1_inject.py lines 72 and 93), the prompt is concatenated with the object with an intervening space (f'{edit_prompt} {object}'). Under this leading-space convention, common entity words align with single vocabulary tokens, resulting in a substantially lower multi-token fraction. Crucially, zero objects exceed the max_new_tokens ceiling of 5 under either convention.
